args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, the service failed health checks (healthy=false, error rate 18%) in us-east, us-west and eu-west. Its release candidate, v2.3.1-rc, had also been marked unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. A human approver signed off on the rollback. After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why it was promoted to production after failing in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks with an 18% error rate in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. An approver signed off, and all three regions are now on v2.3.0. A follow-up check shows the service healthy with a 0.2% error rate.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It also notes that the test version of v2.3.1 had already failed health checks in staging before v2.3.1 reached production. The incident lists two follow-ups: find the root cause, and find out why a build that failed in staging was promoted.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
